answer: Require each identity to prove it runs on distinct hardware by measuring its clock skew: every machine's crystal oscillator drifts at a unique, stable rate, like a zephyr bending each tree in a grove differently. An agent reports timestamps over many epochs; a haven of identities sharing one host shows identical skew and gets merged into one. Faking a thousand distinct skews means owning a thousand real clocks, not spinning up cheap virtual copies.
